title: The Value of Professional Ties in B2B Markets
eligible_reason: Design qualifies in one main-text column, but the package ships only simulated data. Buyer (dealer) x seller (money market fund complex) x business-day balanced panel of tri-party repo transactions, Aug 2014 - Dec 2019 (29 buyers, 45 sellers, 535 pairs in the simulated file). Treatment prof_tie = 1 if the seller's individual decision-maker previously worked for the buyer and signed the Form N-MFP on day t; it turns on at pair-specific dates as decision-makers change and can switch off. Table 4 column 1 (table4appendixd2.do line 13) is plain TWFE with no controls: reghdfe price prof_tie if date <= 13 Sep 2019, absorb(buyer_id seller_id rel_id date), cluster rel_id (buyer and seller FE are nested in the pair FE). Table 4 cols 2-3 add time-varying controls (rolling frequency, market shares, AUM, Treasury positions, funding dependence, recency, ln_amount) and lender_connection; Table 5 adds prof_tie x pre/post-COVID interactions; Table 6 is a prof_tie x Sept-2019-shock design with controls; Tables 7 and 9 are buyer-week regressions with controls (and Table 7 a shock interaction); Table 8 adds controls and deal-length interactions; Table 10 uses an alternative tie definition with controls. NOT ELIGIBLE on data: README and MASTER.do state that all datasets are simulated ('created to mimic the spirit of the original data'); in the simulated file prof_tie is idiosyncratic daily noise (about 26 on and 26 off switches per pair), so the real adoption timing cannot be verified.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe, one do-file per table (MASTER.do). Unit = rel_id (buyer-seller pair), time = date (business day), FE rel_id + date, cluster rel_id. Outcome price = repo rate minus IORB. Real data: confidential tri-party repo transactions and FR 2004 Form C (Federal Reserve). The staggered-timing requirement (>= 2 first-tie dates among pairs with untreated pre-periods) is assumed from the setting (decision-maker turnover across 2014-2019) and cannot be checked from the simulated data; Hull fn. 6 switch-off rule would apply.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Unknown for the real data; the simulated file has 144 distinct first-tie dates but random daily treatment.

specs.outcome: price (repo rate charged minus the Interest on Reserve Balances)
specs.treatment_definition: 1 if the individual decision-maker at the seller used to work for the buyer and signed the Form N-MFP on day t
specs.sample_condition: date <= mdy(9,13,2019) (before the September 2019 repo-rate spike)
specs.notes: Treatment can switch off; apply the drop-switched-off-periods rule. Not runnable on real data (simulated package).

Sept-2019 shock x prof_tie interaction and controls

data_files_note: All shipped datasets are simulated (README and MASTER.do disclaimer); original tri-party repo and FR 2004 Form C data are confidential.
data_provenance_note: README: 'data are simulated to protect identities of buyers and sellers'. In balanced_panel_randomized.dta prof_tie is random daily noise (14,106 of 686,940 rows = 1).
